title: Many US Teens Are Better with Money than Parents
paragraphs: Teenagers often have a reputation for spending money as soon as they get it. But a new survey suggests that many teenagers may actually be better at managing money than their parents — in the US, at least.
The survey, done by Talker Research, asked parents and teenagers aged 13 to 17 about money habits.
It found that almost half of parents believe their teenagers understand money better than they do. And 90% of teenagers also said they're good at managing money!
Most of the teenagers surveyed are already earning their own money. Some get paid for doing jobs around the house, while others have part-time jobs or have found other ways to make money.
On average, they earn almost $7,000 a year.
And rather than spending it all, they save nearly half of it. In fact, 36% of parents said their teenager saves more than they do!
Some parents said their children think more carefully than they do before buying expensive things, and are better at waiting and saving up for something they want.

And it's not just about saving money. About one-third of parents said their teenagers are better at sticking to a budget, knowing the difference between things they want and things they need, and being careful about borrowing money.
Some parents even said their teenagers are better at finding ways to earn extra money and have clearer plans for their financial future.
When asked what they think their lives will look like in 10 years, some teenagers talked about having good jobs, starting businesses or earning enough to support their families.
Not all teenagers have the same dreams, of course. But many seem to be taking money seriously — and their parents might be able to learn a thing or two from them!
